decisive_items: a destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus
response.rationale: Rapidly enlarging destructive maxillary sinus mass with heterogeneous enhancement and fluid-fluid level in a young child is most consistent with rhabdomyosarcoma, the most common pediatric orbital malignancy. Langerhans cell histiocytosis can be destructive but typically less aggressive and lacks the fluid-fluid level prominence. Ewing sarcoma is less common at this site, and orbital cellulitis is excluded by antibiotic failure and destructive imaging.

rejected.why: Persistent swelling despite antibiotics and destructive lesion on imaging contradict infection.
Ewing sarcoma is possible but less typical for this location and age; lacks specific supportive features beyond destructive mass.
Duplicate of Ewing sarcoma with even less support; same reasoning as R2.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis can be destructive but rapid enlargement and fluid-fluid level favor a more aggressive malignancy like rhabdomyosarcoma.
